newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan warns Taiwan activists not to approach isles.
newsitem.headline: Japan warns Taiwan activists not to approach isles.

text.p: Japanese coastguards said on Monday that they had warned activists aboard a flotilla of protest boats from Taiwan not to sail to a disputed island chain in the East China Sea.

A spokesman for Japan's Maritime Safety Agency said that about 20 boats carrying Taiwanese activists sailed to within about 44 km (27 miles) southwest of the islands, which are called the Senkaku Islands in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese.
"As of 7.30 a.m. (2230 GMT Sunday) about 20 boats were sailing closer to the Senkaku islands," the spokesman said. "We are warning them not to enter Japan's territorial waters."

He said there were no reports of a clash between the coastguards and the activists, who have pledged to carry out what they dubbed the "Diaoyu Island World Cup Fishing Contest", a protest designed to challenge Japan's sovereignty by violating its waters.
Japanese coastguards have mobilised about 60 patrol boats near the disputed islands to bar the protesters from entering into Japan's territorial waters, coastguard sources said.
The activists said they would not rule out landing on the islands. The cluster of uninhabited islands, which lie 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Taiwan, are claimed by Japan, Taiwan and China.
